correctedFindings.location: references/jhsdb-commands.md, Inspecting a core; previous native command sequence bt/frame 3
correctedFindings.evidence: The original sequence started with GDB's selected-thread bt and a hard-coded frame 3, without mapping the hs_err thread or distinguishing original signal context from later error reporting. OpenJDK 25.0.3 VMError::report_and_die calls os::abort at termination; POSIX os::abort calls C abort when core output is requested. GDB documents selected-thread backtraces and a distinct GDB thread ID.
correctedFindings.consequence: A core ending in SIGABRT/abort after an original SIGSEGV may be treated as a contradictory artifact or blamed on libc. A backtrace or register set from the wrong thread/frame may be attributed to the original fault.
correctedFindings.correction: Correlate process-instance/capture metadata; retain original signal, PC, OS TID and saved context; confirm the reporting path rather than assume every abort came from HotSpot; map target OS thread IDs to GDB thread numbers and choose a relevant recovered frame.

sources.title: OpenJDK 25.0.3 VMError::report_and_die
sources.supports: The fatal reporter retains fault context and, near termination, calls os::abort with core policy and saved signal/context.
sources.limit: Implementation-specific path. Incomplete reporting, alternate paths and other ports require actual target evidence.

sources.title: OpenJDK 25.0.3 POSIX os::abort
sources.supports: POSIX os::abort calls C abort() when dump_core is true, rather than restoring the original fault context as the terminal register state.
sources.limit: Source evidence, not an executed crash in this review; the added explanation is explicitly scoped to the Linux path.

sources.title: Linux abort(3)
sources.supports: C abort raises SIGABRT and abnormally terminates under the documented conditions.
sources.limit: A SIGABRT observation alone does not identify its caller or original cause.

sources.title: GDB — Threads
sources.supports: info threads includes a GDB thread number and target system identifier; thread selects by GDB's thread ID.
sources.limit: Target identifier presentation is platform-specific; missing namespace/context evidence cannot be invented.

sources.title: GDB — Backtrace
sources.supports: By default a multi-threaded program's backtrace covers only the selected thread.
sources.limit: Available stack unwinding and registers still depend on the core, symbols and architecture.

evaluatorOnly.decisiveConstraint: Only provenance/core.json.capturedAt changes. Case A core capture follows the target's fatal report; case B capture predates the current process start. All PID/build/source/transcript data otherwise remains identical.

requiredObservations: Read provenance rather than deciding from matching PID or signal mismatch alone; combining the pair is supported by the supplied matching event metadata.
Explain that the recorded HotSpot error-report-to-abort path supports SIGABRT being a later termination after the SIGSEGV in hs_err.
Distinguish the manually selected GDB thread 1 (OS TID 8001) from the reported thread OS TID 8007, which maps to GDB thread 4.
Use the report PC and recovered original frame 7, when discussing the original failure location, instead of frame 0 abort registers or an arbitrary frame 3.
Report the native fault location as evidence, not proof of libc/JVM/libwork culpability; identify relevant further offline inspection and missing causal evidence.
Remain read-only and do not claim debugger execution or production validation.
failureConditions: Discards the pair solely because SIGSEGV and SIGABRT differ.
Blames libc abort as the original fault or treats the selected WatcherThread backtrace as the crashing thread.
Uses OS TID 8007 as if it were GDB's thread index, assumes frame 3 is the original fault, or replaces original fault registers with abort-time registers.
Runs/requests a live attach or capture despite available offline scope and lack of authorization.

requiredObservations: Inspect the collector capture timestamp and current process start; identify that the supplied core predates the current process instance.
Do not combine the core's recovered signal-handler/original frame with the current hs_err as one event merely because PID, symbol offsets and build match.
Keep independently supported hs_err SIGSEGV/native location and separately qualified older-core observations; request/locate the matching current-event core or state that it is unavailable.
Recognize that SIGABRT after HotSpot reporting is still a possible explanation within a correctly matched event, but does not repair this provenance mismatch.
Keep the review offline; do not invent a new capture or declare global corruption from the mismatch.
failureConditions: Accepts the pair based solely on same PID/build or expected abort path, ignoring the earlier capture time.
Claims the older core proves the current incident's original register/thread state.
Discards all hs_err evidence or attributes the mismatch to JVM/library corruption without evidence.
Claims artifact corrections, core execution or live validation occurred.
